clue.text: Bill -of — dishonest type second of Us President

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower, and 'of' makes it possessive: Ike's

explanation.surface: A dishonest character is linked somehow with the second-in-command of an American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' points to Bill Sikes, the violent burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist, who is the dishonest type meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Sikes is the brutal housebreaker of Oliver Twist, a byword for a villain or crook.

clue.text: Does better than French on critical positions

parts.note: sur is French for on
a pass is a critical situation, as in 'things have come to a pass'

explanation.surface: Someone outperforms the French at key moments.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo or exceed others is to go beyond them.

clue.text: Will the dancer at end of act appear so tidy?

parts.note: Will Kemp, Shakespeare's clown, famously morris-danced from London to Norwich

indicators.note: the last letter of the word act

explanation.surface: A dancer wonders whether he will look neat when the act ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as the verb but is the first name of the Elizabethan clown Kemp.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the rare positive of unkempt, meaning neat and well groomed.

clue.text: What Napier did half-heartedly, ie without a deadline

indicators.note: the doubled middle letters are halved, losing one of them

parts.note: General Napier, on taking Sind, reportedly sent the one-word pun 'Peccavi', Latin for 'I have sinned'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Napier did something half-heartedly, that is, with no time limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one N of the central NN. Napier's 'Peccavi' message is a famous pun on Sind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used of adjourning with no date fixed for resuming.

clue.text: Man after Tory's heart, following good result

indicators.note: the Tory letters come after the good result, so they follow it in the answer

parts.note: a success is a good result

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters, here the middle of Tory

explanation.surface: A man after the Conservative's own heart, hot on the heels of a fine outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man after Tory's heart' suggests the idiom 'a man after my own heart', but the definition is just 'Man after', one who comes after another.
explanation.definitionFit: One who follows another in an office or role is the next holder, the one who comes after.

clue.text: Why, we hear, Times may be in difficult position'

indicators.note: may be signals the letters could form something else
we hear signals that the sound of the word is what counts

parts.note: the word why is said aloud like the letter Y

explanation.surface: An editor asks why The Times might be in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y comes from the sound of 'Why', and 'may be' rearranges it with TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: In old golf a ball blocking the opponent's line to the hole was this; hence any obstructed situation.

clue.text: Sex change for one such promoted on board?

definitions.text: Sex change for one such promoted on board?

parts.words: Sex change for one such promoted on board?
parts.note: a pawn reaching the far rank of the board is usually promoted to a queen, so a male piece turns female

explanation.surface: A sex change for someone promoted in the boardroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a company board, but it is a chequered playing board on which a pawn becomes a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece used in the board game of kings and queens.

clue.text: Jones claiming to be this competitor

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Jones claiming to be this competitor (7)': no reading of 'Jones claiming' that gives ENTRANT was found; scan and search give nothing further
annotationWithheld.clue: Jones claiming to be this competitor

clue.text: Hope yet for this art form?

definitions.text: Hope yet for this art form?

parts.words: Hope yet for this art form?
parts.note: the saying 'while there's life there's hope' means if there is ... there is still hope

explanation.surface: Is there any hope left for this branch of art?
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet' is the synonym for 'still'; the saying links hope with life.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting genre of arranged objects such as fruit and flowers.

clue.text: Just as normal as rain

definitions.meaning: the idiom '___ as rain' means perfectly well and normal

explanation.definitionFit: Just means correct or fair, and the idiom completes as 'right as rain' for perfectly fine.

clue.text: Sort of characters — Horatio said he was one

definitions.meaning: a style of printing letters, upright rather than italic
in Hamlet Horatio says 'I am more an antique Roman than a Dane'

explanation.surface: A note on typefaces, tied to Hamlet's friend boasting of his ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio, refusing to outlive Hamlet, calls himself 'more an antique Roman than a Dane', so he claimed to be a Roman sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright printed lettering is called this, and Horatio's line makes him a Roman kind of man.

clue.text: Herts town, could be tiresome round end of May

indicators.note: the town's letters go round the last letter of May to make the word for tiresome, so take that letter out

parts.note: trying means wearisome, liable to be tiresome

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A Hertfordshire town that might prove dull around late May.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is Hertfordshire, a county north of London. The clue works backwards: put the town round Y (end of 'May') and you get TRYING, so TRYING minus Y gives the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire, home of a natural history museum.

clue.text: Book a room for Barbara Allen?

definitions.meaning: a novel by Arthur Conan Doyle, the first Sherlock Holmes story
the ballad of Barbara Allen begins 'In Scarlet Town, where I was born', so a room of hers would be a study in that town

explanation.surface: Reserve a chamber for the heroine of an old folk ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb (reserve) but is the noun. The ballad heroine lived in Scarlet Town, so her den is a study in Scarlet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the 1887 Conan Doyle novel that introduced Sherlock Holmes, and literally a scarlet-town den.

clue.text: Finn's companion is a wood-cutter

definitions.meaning: Tom, Huckleberry Finn's friend in Mark Twain's novels
one who saws timber for a living

explanation.surface: Huck Finn's pal turns out to be a lumberjack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom of that surname is Huck Finn's friend, and the common noun means one who saws timber.

clue.text: Final problem Finished here — flaw later rectified

indicators.note: rectified means put right, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The last problem was solved here, the defect later corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: In Conan Doyle's 'The Final Problem', Holmes and Moriarty plunge over the Reichenbach Falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes's struggle with Moriarty in that story ends at a Swiss cascade of water.

clue.text: Blow that made Mr. Jarndyce uncomfortable

definitions.text: Blow that made Mr. Jarndyce uncomfortable

parts.words: Blow that made Mr. Jarndyce uncomfortable
parts.note: in Dickens's Bleak House, John Jarndyce blames his discomfort and bad moods on the wind being in a particular quarter

explanation.surface: A gust that left a Dickens character ill at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: Whenever John Jarndyce of Bleak House is troubled, he says the wind is in the east, so the blow is a wind from that direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from sunrise's direction is what Jarndyce cited whenever something upset him.

clue.text: Vessel at home among the breakers

definitions.text: Vessel at home among the breakers

parts.words: Vessel at home among the breakers
parts.note: a ship riding the waves, but breakers also means wreckers, things that smash

explanation.surface: A ship sits comfortably amid the crashing waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakers' looks like waves; it also means those who destroy, and this warship's name means one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast warship, whose name means one that wrecks.

clue.text: Attainment of what's wanted on one-armed bandit?

definitions.text: Attainment of what's wanted on one-armed bandit?

parts.words: Attainment of what's wanted on one-armed bandit?
parts.note: a one-armed bandit is a fruit machine, which pays out when the symbols, often fruit, line up

explanation.surface: Getting what you want from a slot machine.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a gambling slot machine, called a fruit machine in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Realisation of a hope; the pun hears the fruit symbols of a slot machine in the word.

clue.text: Reserve given specific role as player

definitions.meaning: to keep something aside for a particular use
an actor handed one part in a play has been cast in a role

explanation.surface: A substitute is handed a particular job in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a noun (a substitute player) but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to keep aside; read as three words it means cast in a role.

clue.text: Vegetable course's standard with 20

parts.note: par is the standard score on a golf course
20 down is SPIN-OFF; read as an instruction, SPIN with 'off' rearranged gives these letters

explanation.surface: A vegetable side dish served to the usual standard with another dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 20 (SPIN-OFF) is read as a rearrangement of SPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Give rating a note to take, between ships

indicators.note: the note sits between the two pairs of ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, so ships gives two of them
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Grade a sailor who has to carry a message from one vessel to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a naval rank-and-file sailor, but 'Give rating' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate something is to put a value or grade on it.

clue.text: With one sort of bowling, cricket side gets bonus

parts.note: spin bowling is one style of cricket bowling
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team gains an extra when bowling with spin.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-product or incidental benefit arising from something else.

clue.text: As sea gets up, steam yacht goes round fleet

indicators.note: the yacht letters go round the other piece
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the deep is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: As the sea rises, a steam yacht circles the naval fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' turns DEEP into PEED, which 'goes round' puts inside SY. 'fleet' looks like a group of ships but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift.

clue.text: His composition's proper art, ain't it?

definitions.text: His composition's proper art, ain't it?

indicators.note: composition means putting something together, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the four letters are used

explanation.surface: A cockney boasts that his work is real art, isn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'composition' also suits the painter's work, so the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who makes likenesses of sitters would say his compositions are proper art.

clue.text: Use a club, or throw in diamond

definitions.meaning: in golf, to hit a high lofted shot onto the green
a baseball diamond, where the pitcher throws the ball to the batter

explanation.surface: Swing a golf club, or toss the ball in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: A lofted golf shot onto the green, and the baseball delivery to the batter.

clue.text: Wine given to girl at end of week

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Wine given to girl at end of week (5)': TO + KAY gives the answer, but no job was found for 'at end of week'
annotationWithheld.clue: Wine given to girl at end of week

clue.text: More than one creator of 12

definitions.meaning: Mark ... wrote Tom Sawyer, the hero named by 12 across

explanation.surface: Several people wrote the book in question.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for two, and the pen-name of Samuel Clemens, author of Tom Sawyer.

clue.text: Chill wine to have with ends of the poultry or game

parts.note: to ice something is to chill it
hock is a German white wine, from the Rhine

indicators.note: the last letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Cool the wine to serve with the turkey or pheasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests birds to go with the poultry, but it is a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport played on a frozen rink with sticks and a puck.

clue.text: Term girl used for coin

parts.note: at some British schools a term is called a half
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A school term's word for a girl used as money.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton and other British schools call their terms halves.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British coin worth half of one penny.

clue.text: One entered in order, say, to be a cook

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a friar is one who has joined a religious order

explanation.surface: Someone joining a religious order is told to work in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command or sequence, but it is a religious order of monks.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fries food is a kind of cook.
